slot.subtopic: Stability of alkenes / heat of hydrogenation
slot.brief: Rank three unsymmetrical alkenes by heat of hydrogenation or Markovnikov addition; ask which alkene gives a specified single product on hydrogenation.

stem: The three alkenes below hydrogenate completely to the same alkane. Which sequence gives decreasing magnitude of heat released?

verdicts.working: Heat of hydrogenation magnitude decreases as alkene stability increases. Stability rises with substitution: 3-methylbut-1-ene < 2-methylbut-1-ene < 2-methylbut-2-ene. Thus the heat released decreases in the order given in (A).

working:
Alkene stability: $\text{2-methylbut-2-ene} > \text{2-methylbut-1-ene} > \text{3-methylbut-1-ene}$; heat released on hydrogenation varies inversely with alkene stability.

Independent check: Heat of hydrogenation magnitude decreases as alkene stability increases. Stability rises with substitution: 3-methylbut-1-ene < 2-methylbut-1-ene < 2-methylbut-2-ene. Thus the heat released decreases in the order given in (A).
solution:
Alkene stability increases with the degree of substitution: $\text{2-methylbut-2-ene} > \text{2-methylbut-1-ene} > \text{3-methylbut-1-ene}$. Since heat released on hydrogenation varies inversely with alkene stability,
$$|\Delta H|: \text{3-methylbut-1-ene} > \text{2-methylbut-1-ene} > \text{2-methylbut-2-ene}.$$
